approach: Write the rain's true velocity in horizontal and vertical parts, use the first condition to fix the horizontal part, then the second condition to fix the vertical part.

steps.text: Let the rain's true velocity have horizontal part v_x and vertical part v_y (downward). At 3 km/h the rain appears vertical, so the man's speed cancels the horizontal part of the rain.
At 6 km/h the rain appears at 45° to the vertical, so the horizontal and vertical parts of the relative velocity are equal in size.
The speed of the rain is the size of its full velocity vector.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the rain's horizontal speed as 6 km/h instead of 3 km/h, using the second walking speed instead of the first, gives a wrong vertical speed.
